summary: The SQL-only rename left catalog metadata and dbt schema declarations under daily_revenue. Patched the new model’s description, owner, and grain; lifecycle and canonical status require review.

findings.claim: The catalog still marks daily_revenue active and canonical although the proposed change removes that model and replaces it with revenue_daily.

evidence.fact: daily_revenue has lifecycle active and canonical true.
Removes daily_revenue.sql and adds revenue_daily.sql with identical SQL.
daily_revenue has no model node. revenue_daily depends on stg_orders and has no downstream nodes.

action.rationale: Review marking daily_revenue retired and noncanonical, recording revenue_daily as its replacement, and updating the stale schema declarations. Lifecycle changes require a proposal under the issue contract.

findings.claim: The replacement model lacks lifecycle and canonical metadata.

evidence.fact: There is no revenue_daily entry; daily_revenue is active and canonical.
The new override supplies description, owner, and grain only.
Metadata declarations remain attached to daily_revenue.
revenue_daily is an enabled model with empty config.meta.

action.rationale: Propose lifecycle active and canonical true for revenue_daily, coordinated with retirement of the old catalog identity.

findings.claim: The renamed model initially had no catalog description.

evidence.fact: Only daily_revenue carries the completed-order revenue description.
daily_revenue has the same description; revenue_daily has no declaration.
The replacement preserves the completed-status filter, date grouping, order count, and amount sum exactly.

action.value: Completed-order revenue at one row per order date; refunded and cancelled orders are excluded.
action.rationale: Carry forward the existing repository description because the rename preserves its supporting SQL.

verification.equals: Completed-order revenue at one row per order date; refunded and cancelled orders are excluded.

findings.claim: The renamed model initially had no catalog owner.

evidence.fact: daily_revenue is owned by finance-analytics; revenue_daily is absent.
revenue_daily has empty config.meta, including no owner.
The old model is replaced by an identically defined model under the new name.

action.rationale: Preserve the explicitly documented owner across the SQL-identical rename.

findings.claim: The renamed model initially had no catalog grain.

evidence.fact: daily_revenue declares grain [order_date]; revenue_daily is absent.
daily_revenue declares order_date as its grain; revenue_daily has no declaration.
The model groups only by order_date, preserving the prior model’s aggregation grain.

action.rationale: Restore the documented grain supported directly by the unchanged aggregation.

unresolved_questions: Should daily_revenue be retired and made noncanonical, with revenue_daily designated active and canonical?
Will the change author move the daily_revenue schema declarations and date tests to revenue_daily? The manifest shows the old tests disabled and no tests attached to the replacement.

changes_made.description: Added revenue_daily description, owner, and grain using the documented predecessor and SQL-identical rename.

verification_performed.command: python JSON assertions over project/catalog/catalog.json, project/catalog/overrides.json, project/target/manifest.json, project/models/revenue_daily.sql, and input.diff
verification_performed.result: Passed: override contains only the scoped asset and three permitted fields; merged values equal the reported patches; removed, added, and manifest SQL match exactly.

verification_performed.command: python manifest inspection of model nodes, parent_map, child_map, and test dependencies
verification_performed.result: Confirmed old model absent, replacement depends on stg_orders, replacement has no downstream nodes or attached tests, and old date tests are disabled.

verification_performed.command: python read-only DuckDB query: select count(*) as sampled_rows, count(distinct order_date) as distinct_dates, count(*) filter (where order_date is null) as null_dates from (select order_date from main.revenue_daily limit 10000) s
verification_performed.result: Returned 4 rows, 4 distinct dates, and 0 null dates. Warehouse opened read-only.
